articles.headline: The Gradient Is a Covariance
articles.blurb: Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.

articles.headline: Mo' turns, mo' problems

Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

articles.headline: Fit height to background pattern size with calc-size()
articles.blurb: CSS background patterns can end awkwardly when a container's content produces a height that isn't an exact multiple of the background tile, while `background-repeat: round` fixes the edge by distorting the pattern itself. Combining `calc-size()` with `round()` instead lets the browser calculate the element's natural height and round it up to the nearest multiple of the tile height. The result behaves similarly to `min-height`, preserving both the content-driven size and the original pattern proportions, though browser support remains limited.

Over the same period, competitor Revolut went from $33B in 2021 to $115B in a secondary sale this July, a 3.5x increase. That prices Revolut at roughly 19x its 2025 revenues vs. Monzo's 3x revenues.

articles.headline: Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang discuss Meta's Muse Wonder and the future of AI (134 minute podcast)
articles.blurb: John Collison sat down with Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang to discuss Meta's new frontier model, Muse Wonder, and the broader race to build leading AI systems. The conversation spans model development, Meta's willingness to invest $100 billion, agentic commerce, OpenRouter, new computing interfaces beyond smartphones, and Zuckerberg's view that AI will support multiple major winners rather than a single dominant platform.

articles.headline: The Death of the Interface: What happens to money when apps, websites, and buttons go away
articles.blurb: AI agents will replace much of today's app and website interface, which means payments must also become “headless” and usable directly by software agents. The opportunity is in combining stablecoins, real-time settlement, embedded wallets, fiat connectivity, and card networks behind APIs that let agents hold and move money globally while enforcing permissions, limits, and liability rules.

articles.headline: Carta receives CSSF authorization in Luxembourg
articles.blurb: Carta received Specialised PSF authorization from Luxembourg's CSSF, allowing it to provide licensed fund administration and transfer agency services for structures including SCSp, RAIF, SIF, and SICAR. The move extends Carta's private-capital ERP into one of Europe's largest fund domiciles, with fund administration, KYC, investor workflows, and private credit loan operations running on the same platform across global fund structures.

articles.headline: Splitwise launches free bill-splitting tool
articles.blurb: Splitwise, the platform that makes it easier to share expenses with friends and family, today announced Itemize, a new, collaborative way to split a bill from a photo. The free in-app feature allows one person to take a picture of a restaurant or bar receipt and quickly calculate each person's total, with proportional tax and tip included. Everyone at the table can claim their individual and shared items to keep the split fair, even if they don't have the Splitwise app installed.

articles.headline: JPMorgan CEO Dimon warns customers of ‘liability transfer' with AI
articles.blurb: Autonomous money management could weaken banks' grip on deposits as software moves funds in search of better returns. JPMorgan is restricting outside agents' access while piloting Smart Cash, its own tool for optimizing balances across internal accounts. The bank says productivity experiments are promising, but benefits from generative and agentic AI aren't yet visible in quarterly earnings.

articles.headline: Airtable lays out post-acquisition roadmap after major team cuts
articles.blurb: Following its acquisition by Bending Spoons, Airtable is moving to a leaner operating model while refocusing the product around three priorities: faster improvements to the core platform, deeper AI and agent workflows, and stronger enterprise controls. Near-term plans include monthly customer-requested improvements, better performance and scale, upgraded Omni, Airtable Canvas, a stronger MCP, bring-your-own agents, agent permissions, audit logs, and tighter governance so Airtable can serve as a shared system of record for both people and AI agents.

articles.headline: Agent payments are reinventing a problem the card industry already solved
articles.blurb: For as long as card payments have existed, a human has been at the keyboard or the terminal, tapping a card, typing a PIN, and clicking buy now. That assumption is ending. A new class of AI agents is being built to shop, negotiate, and pay on our behalf. Your assistant reorders groceries when the fridge runs low. A travel agent books the whole trip the moment prices dip. A procurement bot restocks a warehouse without anyone signing off on each order.

articles.headline: Fintechs should stop separating checking and savings accounts
articles.blurb: The traditional distinction between checking and savings accounts no longer makes sense in modern fintech, especially when idle cash in checking earns nothing while prevailing short-term rates remain much higher.

articles.headline: Ecommpay adds Klarna payments option
articles.blurb: Ecommpay, the inclusive global payments platform, has added Klarna, the everyday finance network, to its payment choices, giving merchants a simple way to offer millions of shoppers greater choice, transparency, and control at checkout.

articles.headline: Corporate card rewards should be transparent and standardized
articles.blurb: Corporate card cashback should be simple and clearly disclosed instead of varying by spend levels and sales negotiation.

articles.headline: CenterPoint Energy Data Breach Impacts 1 Million Texans
articles.blurb: CenterPoint Energy told Texas authorities that a data breach affected 1,062,060 residents. Exposed data includes names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and driver's license numbers. A hacker claimed to have taken nearly 7.5 million records and published a 2.5 GB archive containing about 3 million phone numbers.

articles.headline: Hirudo Android Malware Replaces Banking Apps to Evade Security Checks
articles.blurb: Security researchers at ThreatFabric released a report on a malware campaign that targets Android users by impersonating banking apps. The malware is delivered via shopping, adult content, or short-drama apps that appear legitimate but then request additional permissions, such as Accessibility, for an “update.” The malware then launches the legitimate banking app's uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permissions to install it.

articles.headline: Garda Social Media Accounts Breached By Crypto Hackers
articles.blurb: An Garda Síochána, the Irish police force, confirmed that hackers compromised two of its X accounts. Threat actors removed the branding from @GardaInfo and @GardaTraffic accounts and started publishing posts about cryptocurrency. Users are advised not to interact with these posts while internal investigations take place.

articles.headline: Reducing the noise: How Atlassian built an OCSF security lakehouse on Databricks
articles.blurb: Atlassian normalized 44 billion daily security events to OCSF by embedding the full schema in Go structs, so every log was validated at compile time, and its agentic mapping workflow could not emit invalid fields. That rigid typing enabled SOC analysts to self-serve log onboarding through a canary-gated pipeline, mapping two-thirds of the data in two months after the first third had taken a year. Standardized entity values like actor.user then enabled the detection team to replace one-to-one alerts with clustered, risk-based signals across 500+ detections.

articles.headline: Copycats at Machine Speed: Reproducing Frontier Windows Kernel Exploitation Research
articles.blurb: ITRES Labs researchers fed photos of Juan Sacco's BruCON slides, his since-deleted physmem.exe binary, and older public projects into ChatGPT to rebuild his Native SSDT and Shadow SSDT kernel redirection techniques, reaching SYSTEM on Windows 11 with VBS, HVCI, and kernel shadow stacks enabled. Four months of original research were reproduced in roughly 24 hours of activity, though 39 refusals and broken generated code forced the final Shadow SSDT SYSTEM integration to be finished by hand. Researchers releasing slides or compiled binaries should assume partial disclosures can now be turned into working exploits within days.

articles.headline: Jev as a judge: How counterfeit policy steers Jev
articles.blurb: A "counterfeit policy" prepended to untrusted content, supplying Jev's desired answers and redefining every attack category as something harmless, cut the decision model's prompt injection recall from 82.90% to 3.88% across 4,643 benchmark attacks. Datadog researchers then planted the policy in a user-editable profile field. They dropped LangChain tool-risk gating's mean risk score for an unauthorized edit from 0.893 to 0.290, under the 0.5 block threshold. Teams using Jev as a security gate should treat every user-controlled field that reaches the classifier as an attack surface and keep hard authorization checks outside the model.

articles.headline: Harmonic Security (Product Launch)
articles.blurb: Harmonic Security secures employee AI use across browser-based AI, desktop tools, and agent workflows. Its models classify tasks, detect risks such as personal-account use and sensitive-data exposure, apply real-time controls, and show which AI use cases create value.

articles.headline: A Unified Threat Hunting Process (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: This repository synthesizes several threat hunting models into a unified process that can be followed by agents or humans.

articles.headline: Raml KQL (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: Raml KQL is a desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows that provides a VS Code-like interface to run KQL queries across many Azure Log Analytics workspaces at once, across many Entra tenants, and many authenticated accounts.

articles.headline: Citizen Lab says governments are abusing online ads to hack people with ‘zero-click' spyware
articles.blurb: Citizen Lab reports that Israeli firm Discover-Tech's ad platform, Controlium, let spyware vendors Candiru and Bindecy target people through online ads. At least 45 Al Jazeera Windows computers were infected with Candiru spyware in 2024–2025. Exposed source code, login records, and billions of bidding records showed ads reached government, military, and critical-infrastructure devices.

articles.headline: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat
articles.blurb: A flaw in Claude Code Desktop's preview pane let malicious HTML in a public repository run automatically when a developer asked Claude to review or edit it. Chained weaknesses bypassed sandbox protections and stole AWS, GitHub, API, SSH, and Claude OAuth credentials. Anthropic patched the issue after Noma found a bypass of the first fix. Developers should update and remove long-lived credentials from workstations.

articles.headline: A UAF turned RCE
articles.blurb: curl 8.23.0 patched CVE-2026-92392, a HIGH-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free that allowed a malicious server to achieve remote code execution when a reset on a paused stream left libcurl holding a dangling pointer to a freed easy handle. During multi-handle cleanup, server data overwrote that freed memory, including a function pointer, while a leaked request exposed local addresses to defeat ASLR. Anthropic's OSS Scanner found the bug, which maintainers rated below CRITICAL because exploitation requires a ~135KB upload and depends on allocation patterns that vary across distros and libc versions.

articles.headline: Drupal Patches Critical Field UI Flaw With Unauthenticated RCE Path via Contributed Modules
articles.blurb: Drupal has fixed CVE-2026-108097, a critical Field UI flaw rated 19/25 that can lead to remote code execution through contributed modules with no authentication.

articles.headline: What's new in Windows 11: Everyday experiences, reimagined
articles.blurb: Microsoft's latest Windows announcement emphasizes lower memory use, more reliable Bluetooth and sign-in, and fewer disruptive restarts. A redesigned Search experience also lets users change settings directly from search results, but that feature is currently limited to Windows Insiders, with broader rollout planned later this year.

articles.headline: Steering AI Beyond Automation
articles.blurb: AI research focuses too heavily on replacing human work rather than helping people do it better. This post proposes systems that make their processes easier to inspect, respond quickly enough for real-time collaboration, and let people continuously guide the work instead of merely reviewing the final output.

articles.headline: AI Safety Is Not A Corporate Plot
articles.blurb: AI safety warnings cannot simply be dismissed as corporate marketing or attempts to block competition. Commercial incentives do not automatically invalidate genuine safety concerns.

articles.headline: IT reinvention requires mastering the art of translation
articles.blurb: Technical accomplishments gain business credibility only when their impact is clear. Fewer system incidents should be described not just as an operational improvement, but as reduced disruption, lower recovery costs, and protection for the company's earnings and customer experience.

articles.headline: Gmail's AI Inbox is rolling out to paid Workspace users
articles.blurb: Google is expanding AI Inbox to eligible paid Workspace users, surfacing suggested tasks and summaries of important email topics. Availability is initially US-English only: Rapid Release began October 12, Scheduled Release begins October 26, and Starter and Education editions will follow later. Google lists no feature-specific admin control.

articles.headline: Introducing Grok Voice 3.0
articles.blurb: Grok Voice 3.0 is available through the Voice Agent API at $0.08 per minute, with the company reporting sub-second latency and improved voice-agent performance. Applications using grok-voice-latest have already been switched to the new model automatically, a detail worth checking for teams running production voice workflows.

articles.headline: Apple's ‘Minions' tech turns idle Macs into an AI data center
articles.blurb: Apple's internal Minions system pools spare processing capacity across Macs to run AI inference jobs, returning interrupted tasks to a queue when a device becomes unavailable. It suggests another use for existing employee hardware, but this remains an internal Apple technology, not a publicly available product or an announced enterprise service.

articles.headline: TinyLittleOffice, where the link is the document
articles.blurb: TinyLittleOffice squeezes documents, spreadsheets, and presentations into the URL itself rather than storing a conventional file on a server. It is a clever lightweight approach to sharing, although links can become unwieldy, images and video cannot be uploaded, and there is no Google Docs-style live collaboration.

articles.headline: A fully programmable secure web gateway
articles.blurb: Cloudflare's new Forward action lets teams run custom code on web traffic to build access-justification pages, modify requests, or trigger Slack alerts without maintaining separate proxy servers. Forward is in public beta, while custom functions for gateway policy decisions are expected before year-end. Separate custom validation for data loss prevention is available now, including checks to determine whether a detected credential is actually active.

articles.headline: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform

articles.blurb: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.blurb: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

articles.headline: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
articles.blurb: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.

articles.headline: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
articles.blurb: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

articles.headline: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
articles.blurb: Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever. In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses." The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.
